The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 17.11.2024.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.11.2024 at about 10.00 a.m., the petitioner was pedestrian on extreme left side of the Kolar-Bangalore NH-75 road, carefully and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations, by observing on moving vehicle, near Hosakote town court circle, at that time one Car bearing Reg. No.
UP-14-DS-2641 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came from behind and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grevious injuries.

Immediately, petitioner was taken to Silicon City Hospital, Hoskote, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food,
nourishment and conveyance charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 65 years, the petitioner was doing real estate business and was agriculturist and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.

2 3.
After service of notice, both the respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed written statements.

The respondent No.1 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, the offending Car was duly insured with the 2 nd respondent and the said policy was inforce as on the date of the accident and the driver of the said vehicle has valid and effective Driving License to drive the said Car at the time of accident.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement specifically denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent issued the policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

This respondent denies the involvement of the alleged Car and submitted that, the driver of offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of the accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving license.
The jurisdictional police have filed false charge-sheet against the offending vehicle to help the petitioner to claim wrongful compensation.
Further both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. UP-14-DS-2641 on 17.11.2024 at about 10.00 a.m., on Kolar-  Bangalore NH-75 road, near  Hosakote town court circle,
Bangalore and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13 and examined Dr. S. Ramachandra as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15 and also examined MRO at Silicon City Hospital as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.19 and closed their side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.

ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9.
The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the vehicle seizer mahazar, Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 is the Charge-sheet,
Ex.P.9 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P.11 is the Medical bills, Ex.P.12 is the Prescriptions, Ex.P.13 is the Medical Bills.
10. The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No.UP-14-DS- 2641.
Ex.P.1 to 8 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama and Sketch),
clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information,
held investigation and filed the Ex.P.8, Charge-Sheet against the driver of offending vehicle U/s. 281 and 125(b) of BNS.
The Ex
, certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles in question.

It must be noted that, in the cross- examination of PW.1, it is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the accident had happened because of the negligence on the part of driver of the Car, but witness denied the said suggestion.
No matter whether PW.1 admits the said suggestion or not, but in my opinion, the said suggestion is sufficient to conclude that, respondent No.2 has admitted the accident.
In other words, it is well settled that, suggestion is the reflection of the case of the opponent.

Therefore, in my view, by posing a suggestion to the effect that, the accident had occurred because of the negligence of the driver of Car and the respondent No.2 has admitted that, the accident in question had happened.
12. The next question would be, on whose fault accident has occurred.

This question arises because at para No.6 of the written statement filed by respondent No.2, in which the respondent No.2 has raised the specific defence that, the accident had happened due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Thus, the question would be whether this say of the respondent No.2 can be accepted or not.

It is true that, in the cross-examination of petitioner/PW.1, learned counsel for respondent No.2 Nagaraj C vs Himanshu Sungh on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41138579/
4 has posed question to the PW.1 that, accident is happened due to the negligence of petitioner himself, but PW.1 had denied the said suggestion.
However, it is important to note that, the first respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Further, the first respondent has not adduced any evidence before the Court.
Besides, the respondents have not examined the driver of the aforesaid Car.
Thus, these facts, make it clear that, except allegations, the respondent No.2 has not made any efforts to show that, accident had happened because of the fault of the driver of the Car.
13. As stated above, respondents have not produced any evidence before this court to show that, the accident is not caused due to the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thus, the above discussion makes it clear that, except barred allegations, the respondent No.2 has not made any efforts to show that, the accident had happened because of the fault of the petitioner.
It is well settled that, in Motor vehicle accident compensation cases, the strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view of this Court receives support from the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in (2009)
13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others Vs. HRTC.

Thus, I opine that, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, the accident had happened because of the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. UP-14-DS- 2641.
14.
The next question would be, whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident or not.
It must be noted that, the Ex.P.7 i.e., Wound Certificate shows that, the petitioner was admitted to Silicon City Hospital on 17.11.2024.
Further, Wound Certificate shows that, the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.

Further, in the said Wound Certificate it is mentioned that,
petitioner admitted to the hospital with alleged history of RTA.
These facts are not denied by the respondent No.2.
Hence, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
16. PAIN AND SUFFERING:
In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 17.11.2024 to 21.11.2024.

The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Silicon City Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for totally 04 days.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7,
which reveals that, petitioner has sustained the Degloving injury of left foot with undisplaced fracture of base of 5 th metatarsal and the doctor has opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.25,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
17. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
However in support of his plea, he has produced medical bills which is marked at Ex.P.11 and 13 to the tune of Rs.80,470/-.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and Nagaraj C vs Himanshu Sungh on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41138579/
5 treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.80,470/-
towards medical expenses.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 Discharge summary issued by Silicon City Hospital, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital for about 04 days.
Hence, at least 01 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was doing real estate Business and earning Rs.30,000/- per month
, in support of his income he has not produced any single document.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,500/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2024 at Rs.16,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

sentences.text: The accident is of the year is 2024.

Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/-
p.m. as per above decision.
Hence, 01 month is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500/- under this head.
19. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-
The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. S. Ramachandra in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 has produced documents marked at Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15.
Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor.

He was sworn that, petitioner has got Disability of 8%
to the whole body, but he has not issued the disability certificate.
In addition to that, during cross- examination PW.1 depose that, he can walk freely with some difficulty.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor and evidence given by the petitioner herself before the Court, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 5%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 5%.

Further,
petitioner also examined MRO at Silicon City Hospital as PW.3, who has produced medical records,
which shows that petitioner was admitted in the said hospital as inpatient and took treatment, but his evidence is formal in nature.
Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.10 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his year of birth is mentioned as 1961 and accident took place in the year 2024.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 63 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page- 3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '7'.

sentences.text: Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.69,300/-.
20. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:

Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Manipal Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 17.11.2024 to Nagaraj C vs Himanshu Sungh on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41138579/
6 21.11.2024 i.e., for 04 days.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 63 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
However he might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and fracture, Rs.10,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 25,000/-
2

Medical expenses Rs. 80,470/-
3 Loss of future earning, Rs. 69,300/-
Disability 4 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 16,500/-
up period 5

Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 10,000/-
 loss of happiness
Total Rs
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,31,270/- under various heads.
22. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. UP-14- DS-2641 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle punishable U/s 281 and 125(b) of BNS.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 01.08.2024 to 31.07.2025.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 17.11.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
23. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.2,31,270/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, entire amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded  amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

The advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
 Draw award Accordingly.
